name: spatial_cross_feeding_bridge
title: Spatial cross-feeding bridge
claim: Strain A grows on glucose and secretes acetate that diffuses to strain B on the no-glucose side, producing a small, acetate-dependent growth increment in B that does not occur when A is absent — an emergent, spatially-localized cross-feeding dependency (the effect is modest: B grows ~1.6% over the run).

purpose.question: Does a spatially-separated consumer (strain B) grow only where a producer (strain A) secretes a diffusing metabolite?
purpose.mechanism: Spatial dFBA strain A (glucose side) secretes acetate; a diffusing acetate field bridges to acetate-only strain B on the no-glucose side.
purpose.expected_outcome: B's biomass overlaps the acetate field more than glucose; with A absent, no acetate forms and B stays flat.

question: Does strain B grow only where strain A's secreted acetate diffuses to it?

behavior_tests.name: N1-B-TRACKS-ACETATE-BRIDGE
behavior_tests.description: strain B biomass overlaps the acetate field more than the glucose field (it grows on the diffused acetate, not glucose).

behavior_tests.name: N1-A-SECRETES-AND-GROWS
behavior_tests.description: strain A grows on glucose (producing the acetate bridge).

behavior_tests.name: N1-CONTROL-B-FLAT-WITHOUT-A
behavior_tests.description: with strain A absent, no acetate forms and strain B does not grow (the control that the bridge is real).

findings.statement: Strain B grows only when strain A is present to secrete acetate: with A, B's biomass overlaps the diffused acetate field and increases modestly (~1.6%); with A absent, no acetate forms and B stays flat. The A-absent control is the decisive evidence that the small increment is A's acetate bridge, not residual glucose or incidental growth. The magnitude is small (acetate is a poor carbon source) — the claim is about the spatial dependency, not the yield.

falsifiability: If strain B grew equally with and without strain A, or overlapped glucose rather than acetate, the cross-feeding-bridge claim would be false.
limitations: B's absolute growth is modest (acetate is a poor carbon source); the claim is about the spatial dependence, not the yield.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: B grows on residual glucose, not A's acetate.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Glucose is seeded only on A's side; the A-absent control (same glucose) yields no B growth.

resolved: A spatially-separated consumer grows only on a producer's diffused metabolite — spatial cross-feeding.
remaining: Two further spatial phenomena are deferred: strain demixing/sectoring at an expanding front, and an advection washout transition (the latter did not appear — per-site dFBA growth outpaced transport at feasible advection; it needs a non-growing tracer or a much slower-growth regime).

followup_study_proposals.motivation: Cross-feeding shows spatial metabolic coupling between separated strains; a complementary question is whether competing strains demix into sectors at a growing colony front. Needs strain-tagged particles (strain_particle type) + a dense front.
followup_study_proposals.candidate: comets_br_particles_dfba with two strain-tagged founder populations

followup_study_proposals.motivation: A washout/Peclet survival transition did not appear with growing per-site dFBA (growth always outpaced outflow transport). Revisit with a non-growing biomass tracer or a slow-growth regime so advection can win.
followup_study_proposals.candidate: comets_washout with a non-growing tracer / reduced growth rate
